summary.en: Store declaration information in nested hash tables and resolve names from the nearest visible scope.
summary.bn: একই নাম একাধিক স্কোপে থাকলে তুমি কাছের ঘোষণাটি সিম্বল টেবিল থেকে খুঁজে নেবে।

notes: Python programs use the standard library and were executed with Python 3.12.14.

examples.title: Restore an outer declaration after a block
examples.explanationHtml: The visible declaration changes from depth 1 to depth 0 when the child table is removed.

examples.title: Preserve a declaration after a duplicate error
examples.explanationHtml: The duplicate is rejected before any entry or slot counter changes.

examples.title: Catch unknown names and scope underflow
examples.explanationHtml: Both failed operations leave the global scope available for the final declaration.

practice.title: Interpret scope operations
practice.statementHtml: Read up to 50 command lines: enter, leave, declare NAME TYPE, or lookup NAME. Types are int, real and bool; names are ASCII identifiers. Ignore blank lines. Print Scope commands: first. Enter/leave print entered/left; declaration prints declared NAME DEPTH SLOT; lookup prints NAME TYPE DEPTH SLOT. On failure print error: followed by duplicate: NAME, undeclared: NAME, cannot leave global scope, or bad command. Continue after errors.
hints: Validate a duplicate before incrementing the slot counter.

practice.title: Measure block depth
practice.statementHtml: Read a sequence containing only braces and whitespace, at most 100 characters. Print Braces:, then the maximum nested block depth when braces balance. Print invalid for an unmatched brace or another character. Empty input has depth 0.
hints: Never permit the source block stack to pop the permanent global scope.

practice.title: Resolve nested names
practice.statementHtml: Trace declarations and lookups for int marks; { real marks; int bonus; } marks.
hints: Keep both marks declarations in different dictionaries.
practice.answerHtml:
Start with an empty global dictionary. Process int marks; { real marks; int bonus; } marks. The inner marks deliberately hides the outer marks. Leaving the block restores visibility without changing the outer entry.

Declaration and lookup trace
StepOperationActive scope contentsResult
1declare marks:intglobal {marks:int@0}Entry depth 0, slot 0
2enter blockglobal; inner {}Current depth 1
3declare marks:realglobal; inner {marks:real@0}Legal shadowing
4declare bonus:intglobal; inner {marks:real@0, bonus:int@1}Entry depth 1, slot 1
5lookup marksSearch inner firstreal, depth 1, slot 0
6lookup bonusSearch inner firstint, depth 1, slot 1
7leave blockglobal {marks:int@0}Inner declarations disappear
8lookup marksSearch globalint, depth 0, slot 0
9lookup bonusSearch global, no matchUndeclared-name error

The table describes compile-time visibility. It does not say that a runtime stack object is physically erased when lookup stops seeing it. A language may retain an object through a closure or other reference even after the original block ends. Separate the lifetime of an object from the visibility of its name.

practice.title: Compare environment chains
practice.statementHtml: Distinguish lexical scope, dynamic callers and a runtime static link.
hints: A caller is not necessarily a lexical parent.
practice.answerHtml:
Imagine global x:int, function outer containing x:real, and a separately declared global function show that reads x. Calling show from outer does not make show see outer's local x under lexical scoping. Show was defined globally, so its enclosing source environment supplies the global declaration.

Which chain answers which question?
ChainFollowsUsed for
Lexical scope chainSource-enclosing declarationsResolve a name's declaration
Dynamic call chainFunctions that called one anotherReturn and stack unwinding
Static link in a nested-function runtimeLexically enclosing activationAccess an enclosing local at runtime

The small scope stack models traversal of nested source blocks. Do not use it as a complete runtime implementation for separately declared functions or closures. A real compiler associates each function with its defining environment and emits the necessary access mechanism later.

quiz.prompt: Which dictionary is consulted first during nested name lookup?
options: Caller scope regardless of source nesting
quiz.explanation: The nearest visible lexical declaration wins.

quiz.prompt: What happens to outer marks while inner marks shadows it?
options: It remains in the outer dictionary
quiz.explanation: Shadowing changes lookup visibility without replacing the outer entry.

quiz.prompt: Which operation rejects a duplicate in our model?
quiz.explanation: Declaration checks the current dictionary before inserting.

quiz.prompt: Why is full-chain lookup not always expected O(1)?
options: It may inspect d active scopes
quiz.explanation: Each dictionary lookup is expected constant time, but there can be d dictionaries.
Source structure determines the declaration chosen under lexical scoping.

quiz.prompt: What must a failed declaration preserve?
quiz.explanation: Reject before mutating the table, so later analysis can trust it.

quiz.prompt: Why is a slot number not yet a byte address?
options: Frame layout and alignment are not assigned
Every scope shares the same runtime frame
quiz.explanation: The teaching counter identifies an entry position rather than a target storage location.

quiz.prompt: The inner dictionary hides x. Which type does nearest-scope lookup print?
quiz.explanation: Reversing the scope sequence checks the inner dictionary first.
quiz.code:
scopes = [{"x": "int"}, {"x": "real"}]
print(next(scope["x"] for scope in reversed(scopes) if "x" in scope))

quiz.prompt: After closing the child scope, which x type is visible?
quiz.explanation: Popping removes only the child table.

quiz.prompt: Three declarations enter one scope. What slot belongs to bonus?
quiz.explanation: Slots begin at zero and advance once per successful declaration.

keyPoints.en: A symbol entry records the declaration meant by a name.
keyPoints.bn: নামটি কোন ঘোষণাকে বোঝাচ্ছে, সিম্বল এন্ট্রি তা ধরে রাখে।

keyPoints.en: Lookup searches from the current scope outwards.
keyPoints.bn: নাম খুঁজতে বর্তমান স্কোপ থেকে বাইরের দিকে যাও।

keyPoints.en: A same-scope duplicate is different from an inner shadow.
keyPoints.bn: এক স্কোপে একই নাম দুবার দেওয়া আর ভেতরের স্কোপে দেওয়া আলাদা।

keyPoints.en: Leaving a block reveals the preserved outer declarations.
keyPoints.bn: ব্লক ছাড়লে বাইরের আগের ঘোষণাগুলো আবার দেখা যায়।

keyPoints.en: A scope slot is not automatically a machine address.
keyPoints.bn: স্কোপের স্লট নম্বরকে সরাসরি মেমরি অ্যাড্রেস ভেবো না।

examQuestions.question: Explain duplicate declarations and legal shadowing without corrupting a symbol table.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Suppose the current scope already contains fee:int. Declaring fee:real in that same dictionary is an error. Entering a child scope and declaring fee:real is permitted here. Different languages restrict shadowing differently, so these are source rules you must choose deliberately.

Operations that must preserve existing entries
Initial stateAttemptDecisionState afterwards
Global fee:int at slot 0declare fee:realDuplicate errorfee:int still at slot 0
Global fee:intenter; declare fee:realLegal shadowInner fee:real hides outer fee
Inner fee:realleavePop inner tableGlobal fee:int visible again
Only global table existsleaveScope-underflow errorGlobal table remains
No cost declarationlookup costUndeclared errorNo new entry inserted

A failed declaration must not overwrite the first declaration. Keep its original type and source location so a diagnostic can mention both lines. Likewise, a failed lookup should not insert a placeholder normal variable. Such a placeholder can hide a genuine error in a later use.
